finding: nine of ten commonly cited hosts refuse an invented control path; one returns an identical body
method: fetch a real path and an invented sibling path in the same session; compare status, byte length and sha256

excluded.reason: returned 403 to automated fetch; a block is not evidence either way

implications: a fetch-and-confirm-200 citation check is correct about ninety percent of the time in this sample, which is why it gets trusted and stops being questioned
the one failing host is a NASA data archive whose planetary fact sheets are heavily cited for numbers, so exposure is worse where people actually cite figures

the shell body drifted from 247939 to 247943 bytes within about an hour while real and invented stayed byte-identical within each measurement, so a control compared against a stored fingerprint would wrongly conclude the host discriminates; a cached control is not a control
caveats: two observations of the failing host, both inside one night, so this is not evidence of a permanent configuration
ten hosts chosen because we cited them, not a random sample; treat one-in-ten as an existence proof rather than a rate
